title: Mac and Cheese
subtitle: Baked macaroni in sharp Cheddar béchamel
excerpt: The definitive baked mac and cheese: macaroni in a rich, sharp Cheddar béchamel made with a double hit of cheese and a crisp, golden breadcrumb crust. Properly saucy underneath, properly crunchy on top.

recipe.sourceNotes: Macaroni and cheese has a long history in both British and American cooking; the dish appears in British cookbooks from the late eighteenth century, and Thomas Jefferson is often credited with popularising the dish in the United States after encountering pasta in France and Italy. The baked version with a breadcrumb crust is the American standard; the stovetop version is more common in British cooking. A good mac and cheese requires a well-seasoned, thick béchamel with a significant proportion of mature Cheddar; the sauce should be quite thick before the pasta is added as the pasta will absorb liquid during baking. The breadcrumb crust is essential to the baked version for texture contrast.

content.text: Make the béchamel deliberately thick; it will loosen during baking. Undercook the pasta by 2 minutes before combining with the sauce, as it will continue cooking in the oven. Season the sauce aggressively with salt, mustard, and pepper before baking; the pasta will absorb much of the seasoning.
Cook the macaroni in well-salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the packet instructions. Drain and set aside. Preheat the oven to 200°C / fan 180°C / gas 6.

Melt the butter in a large saucepan. Add the flour and cook for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in the milk over medium heat until smooth. Cook, stirring, for 5 minutes until thick. Remove from the heat and stir in the Cheddar, mustard, salt, pepper, and cayenne. Taste; it should be well seasoned.

Stir the macaroni into the sauce. Transfer to a large baking dish. Mix the panko and Parmesan and scatter over the top. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until bubbling throughout and golden and crisp on top.
